coverageNotes: Tests the membership edge of an indexed join. Outer traversal, user fetching and record accumulation are supplied. Missing-reference policy, independent traversal design and standalone JavaScript deduplication are not assessed.

questions.concept: Follow an indexed relationship using the referenced team ID
questions.context:
Using Convex 1.44.0, a query is building an organization’s admin map. It has already loaded that organization’s teams and is iterating over them. args.organizationId has type Id<"organizations">, and team._id has type Id<"teams">. The installed membership table is:

```ts
teamMembers: defineTable({
  teamId: v.id("teams"), userId: v.id("users"),
  role: v.union(v.literal("member"), v.literal("admin")),
}).index("by_team_role", ["teamId", "role"])
```

Each team may have several admins. Its memberships fit within query limits. The code after this block fetches the referenced users and adds them to the result map.
questions.question: Which block loads the admin memberships for each team?

options.rationale: A role-only range skips the leading teamId index field. It is rejected statically and at runtime.
organizationId identifies an organization, while teamId stores team IDs. The typechecker rejects the incompatible ID type; a bypassed runtime query finds no matching memberships.
take(1) reads at most one admin per team and loses additional admins on the same team.
The range follows each team’s ID, then fixes role to admin and collects all matching memberships. The common code resolves user IDs and deduplicates the record.
